videos.script: A person signs in with a password and a second factor. A program has no phone to receive a code. So how does it prove who it is? {{program}} In Entra ID a program gets two objects. The registration says what the program is. {{registration}} The service principal is the program's identity inside one tenant. Roles go to it, and logs name it. {{principal}} Then comes the proof. A program can hold a secret, which is a password with an expiry date. {{secret}} You will send Entra ID a request with a made-up program and a secret that is plainly not one, and read its refusal. {{refusal}} A certificate is better. The private key never has to leave the machine that made it. {{certificate}} And the best proof holds nothing at all. {{federation}} A pipeline on GitHub shows Entra ID a token GitHub issued. Entra ID checks where it came from, and for which branch. {{exchange}} If both match, the pipeline gets an hour of access, and there was never a secret to leak. {{end}}
